abstract: An executable scalar Monte Carlo posterior-proxy model for the fission neutron release timescale tau_f. The run samples tau_f together with ejecta mass, electron fraction, and inclination nuisance priors using the approved Q2 parameter values. The current trusted adapter reports the sampled tau_f observable and does not claim a full hierarchical likelihood, Markov-chain diagnostic, or empirical posterior.

steps: Initialize the deterministic random generator from the integer seed.
Draw 10000 independent samples from the four declared bounded prior distributions.
Evaluate the scalar observable z=tau_f for every draw.
Report bounded summary statistics for the sampled tau_f values.

assumptions.effect_if_violated: The sampled fission-timescale sensitivity range changes.
assumptions.statement: The approved tau_f value of 2.3 s is used as the center of a positive bounded sensitivity prior from 1.15 s to 3.45 s.
The approved ejecta-mass value of 0.04 solar_mass is represented by a positive bounded interval from 0.03 to 0.05 solar_mass.
The approved electron-fraction value of 0.16 is represented by a broad physically admissible interval from 0.08 to 0.24.
The approved inclination value is represented by the converted 19 to 42 degree interval in radians.

assumptions.effect_if_violated: The result would no longer be the scalar tau_f posterior proxy defined by this model.
assumptions.statement: The current executable observable is the sampled tau_f value; nuisance variables are retained as declared prior variables for later likelihood extension.

boundary_conditions: No spatial boundary conditions apply to this zero-dimensional Monte Carlo sampler.
initial_conditions: The zero-dimensional sampler is initialized by drawing each declared random variable from its validated prior distribution.
limitations: The current trusted adapter evaluates a scalar observable and does not implement a full likelihood.
The declared N_chains and N_temperatures controls are retained for provenance but are not independently executed by the standard adapter.
The output is a numerical simulation result and not empirical evidence.
The nuisance priors are sampled but are not combined through a multi-messenger likelihood in this adapter.
model_scope: A bounded zero-dimensional Monte Carlo posterior-proxy calculation for one kilonova event. The full multi-event hierarchical likelihood, parallel tempering, Bayes-factor estimation, and catalogue-level population aggregation remain outside the current trusted solver.

convergence_checks: repeat the run with a larger sample count outside the current fixed approved baseline

objective_and_constraints: Estimate the scalar sampled distribution of tau_f under the declared bounded nuisance-prior setup.

evidence_locator.quoted_text: At about t approximately 2.3 s, beta-delayed fission becomes the primary fission channel while nuclei are decaying.

entries.selection_rationale: Use the literature timescale at which beta-delayed fission becomes the primary fission channel; treat it as an abundance-weighted kinetic proxy rather than an isotope-specific half-life.

uncertainty.reported: approximately 2.3 s; no formal interval in the quoted passage

conditions.posterior_parameter: event ejecta-mass estimate used as a nuisance-parameter center

evidence_locator.quoted_text: an ejected mass of 0.04 plus-or-minus 0.01 M_sun

entries.selection_rationale: Use the GW170817 ejecta-mass estimate reported in the primary observational study.

source.title: A kilonova as the electromagnetic counterpart to a gravitational-wave source

evidence_locator.quoted_text: a broad electron fraction distribution with a lower average value (0.16)

entries.selection_rationale: Use the representative lower-average electron fraction reported by the merger-disc GRMHD model as the literature prior center; retain the broad-distribution caveat.

source.title: Long-term GRMHD simulations of neutron star merger accretion discs: implications for electromagnetic counterparts

uncertainty.reported: broad distribution; quoted value is the lower average, not a narrow posterior interval

evidence_locator.quoted_text: we find that the viewing angle is 32^{+10}_{-13} plus-or-minus 1.7 degrees (90% confidence, statistical, and systematic errors).

entries.selection_rationale: Use the joint GW-EM viewing-angle median of 32 degrees after conversion to the requested radian execution unit.

source.title: Measuring the Viewing Angle of GW170817 with Electromagnetic and Gravitational Waves

entries.selection_rationale: Human-reviewed Monte Carlo sample-count baseline for the Q2 posterior run.
Human-reviewed number of independent chains for convergence diagnostics.

parameterization: The execution parameter object must contain exactly tau_f=2.3, M_ej=0.04, Y_e=0.16, i=0.5585053606381855, N_samples=10000, N_chains=4, and N_temperatures=8.
The random-variable sensitivity bounds are explicit model assumptions and are numeric literals required by the trusted sampler.
scientific_question: What is the posterior probability distribution of the fission neutron release timescale when gravitational-wave, kilonova photometric, and spectroscopic abundance constraints are combined?
title: Hierarchical Bayesian Inference of Fission Timescales from Multi-Messenger Kilonova Constraints
validation_plan: Verify that the sample count is an integer between 1 and 100000.
Verify that every distribution bound is finite and ordered.
Verify that all observable values are finite.
Verify that the execution parameter object exactly matches the approved parameter set.
